id_policy: Ids are permanent surrogate keys, NOT positions on the list. They are ordered by the year a peak joined: 1-51 are the original 1990 list, 52 joined in 2001, 53 in 2010, 54-58 in 2020, 59-61 in 2025. Never renumber, never reuse. A peak keeps its id when the list is revised, when it is retired, and if it is later restored (see id 60, retired 2020 and restored 2025). New peaks take next_id. Saved progress links encode these ids, so renumbering would corrupt every hiker's saved list.

peaks.name: Eagle Crag
peaks.notes: Open ledges at the north end of the Baldface ridge, above the Wild River valley.

review.raised_by: Ken MacGray, author of New Hampshire's 52 With A View: A Hiker's Guide
review.issue: Eagle Crag is not closely tied to Mt. Meader beyond sharing the range. The stored route, mileage, gain and source link all describe a Meader Ridge traverse, and Mt. Meader is not on the 52 With a View list at all.
review.needs: A standalone Eagle Crag route with its own trailhead, distance and gain, verified against the book.

evidence.source: USFS National Forest System Trails (EDW_TrailNFSPublish_01), queried 2026-08
evidence.reading: Eagle Crag sits on the Baldface Circle Trail, sharing the Rt. 113 trailhead with North and South Baldface and Eastman Mtn. Meader Ridge Trail carries on north to Mt. Meader, which is how the two came to be paired, but it is a continuation rather than the way in.
evidence.caveat: These are whole-trail lengths from the Forest Service GIS, not the distance from any particular trailhead.

peaks.name: Pine Mtn. (Gorham)

routes.name: Pine Mountain Road (walk in; road closed to public driving)

review.raised_by: Ken MacGray, author of New Hampshire's 52 With A View: A Hiker's Guide
review.issue: Route selection needed checking. The stored recommendation starts in Gorham on the assumption that the shorter Pine Mountain Road approach was closed to hikers; in fact the road is only closed to public driving and walking in is welcome.
review.needs: Confirmation of which approach the book treats as standard, and whether the Gorham start should remain the recommended route.

evidence.source: USFS National Forest System Trails (EDW_TrailNFSPublish_01), queried 2026-08
evidence.reading: Pine Mountain Road is itself a Forest Service system route, which supports walking in. Road plus Pine Mountain Trail is about 2.1 mi each way, with the Ledge Trail available to make a loop; the stored 3.5 mi round trip looks short against that.
evidence.caveat: These are whole-trail lengths from the Forest Service GIS, not the distance from any particular trailhead.
